newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Uzbek dissident's son beaten - rights monitors.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek dissident's son beaten - rights monitors.

text.p: An international human rights group on Tuesday blamed Uzbekistan's government for the kidnapping and beating of the son of a leading Uzbek dissident and accused it of a return to "brutal repression" of dissent.

The New York-based Human Rights Watch-Helsinki said Hasan Mirsaidov, the son of dissident Shukhrullo Mirsaidov, was abducted on Saturday by three armed assailants, beaten, threatened with death and released after 12 hours.

Helsinki Watch did not make clear who the three armed men were but said in a statement: "The organisation is calling for a vigorous police investigation and punishment of the assailants, but acknowledges there is little hope of an impartial investigation since the incident was undoubtedly carried out at the behest of the Uzbekistan government."
Shukhrullo Mirsaidov and his son could not be reached immediately for comment in the Uzbek capital Tashkent and there was no word in the country's tightly-controlled state media.
Helsinki Watch said the incident was the sixth attack on the Mirsaidov family since he broke with Uzbek President Islam Karimov in 1993.

Shukhrullo Mirsaidov was the desert state's former vice-president and a former Communist Party apparatchik. Observers say Karimov, the country's ex-Communist Party boss, feared him as a potential rival.
Karimov has ruled the nation with a rod of iron since independence in 1991 and is known as "Papa" among the 23-million population.

The incident comes only weeks after Uzbekistan hosted a human rights seminar and gave another well-known dissident airtime on state radio in September in an effort to polish the country's tarnished human rights image.

Karimov is striving to build better relations with the United States which he sees as the main guarantor of Uzbekistan's five-year-old independence. He visited Washington in June, putting an end to a period of strained relations over human rights issues.
